unit: Students can describe their daily study routines, discuss learning tools, and share advice for building good study habits while balancing school and family life.
objective: Ask teachers or family members for assistance with schoolwork.

title: Warm up
subtitle: Asking for help
question: Who do you ask for help when you can't find the answer online?
starters: When I can't find the answer online, I ask...

title: Useful Language (Part 1)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and ask the student to repeat.
Read the definition and example sentence.
Ask the check question to confirm understanding.
Ask the student to make their own sentence using one of the words.

words.definition: To make something clear or easy to understand.
words.example: Can you explain this math homework to me?
words.check: Who usually explains a new lesson: the teacher or the student?

words.definition: To know what something means or how it works.
words.example: I don't understand this book because the words are too difficult.
words.check: If you understand a new game, is it easy or difficult to play?

title: Useful Language (Part 2)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and ask the student to repeat after you.
Read the definitions and example sentences.
Ask the check questions to confirm understanding.
Ask the student to make their own sentence using one of the words.

words.example: This math homework is very difficult.
words.check: Which is more difficult for you: math or English?

words.definition: Not hard; simple to do or understand.
words.example: The first question on the test was easy.
words.check: Which school subject is easy for you?

words.definition: To say or do something again.
words.example: Can you repeat the answer, please?
words.check: When do you ask a teacher to repeat something: when you understand, or when you don't understand?

title: Conversation Builder
goal: Learn how to ask for help with difficult schoolwork.

linkers.use: To say something is difficult or unclear.
To ask someone to teach or show you how to do something.

model:
A: Hey, I'm having some trouble with my math homework. Can you help me with this problem?
B: Sure, let me take a look.
A: I don't understand this part. Could you explain it to me?
B: No problem, it's actually pretty easy. Let me show you.

your_turn.teacher: Act as an older sibling. Ask the student what they are doing and guide them to use the new phrases to ask for help.
your_turn.student: Role-play with your tutor. Tell them your homework is difficult and ask for help using the new phrases.

title: Let's practice
teacher_question: Imagine you looked up your homework answers online, but the topic is still too difficult. I'll be your older brother or sister. Ask me for help using the sentences below. Choose a subject like math, history, or English.
student_guide: Hey, can you help me with _____?
I searched online, but I still don't understand _____.

title: Real-world scenario
problem: You have a difficult homework assignment. You looked for help online, but you still don't understand it.
mission: Tell your older brother or sister that the homework is difficult.
Say that you don't understand the lesson.
Ask them to explain it to you.
start: Hey! Are you busy right now? I'm really stuck. Can you help me with...

title: Wrap-up
recap: Vocabulary: explain, understand, difficult, easy, repeat
Language chunks: Can you help me with... / I don't understand... / Could you explain...
Skill: Asking teachers or family members for help with schoolwork.
final_task: Tell me in one sentence: Which phrase from today's lesson would you use if your math homework is too difficult?
challenge: Try using these phrases the next time you need help with your schoolwork!
